You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

1. Your action is read only from the plain text of your reply, never from Python output or a tool call: printing JSON in Python or calling a tool named submit/request_demos/finish/answer does nothing. Keep each turn to a few tool calls, then reply in text ending with exactly one of {"action": "request_demos"}, {"action": "submit", "grid": [[ints]]}, {"action": "finish"} on the last line. Replies without a valid action waste the turn, and a few in a row end the puzzle charged in full.
2. When a message says "Decide now" or "could not find a valid action", make no tool call: reply at once in text with the action line. Submit only a grid already printed above (copy it); otherwise send {"action": "request_demos"}. You have not submitted anything until you see a verdict message.
3. With no demo pair yet, request_demos first: the test input alone cannot show the rule, so never submit before seeing a demo.
4. Never retype grids. Load every grid shown so far (rerun after each new demo):
```
import os,glob,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])   # this instance's own log: the folder keeps every earlier one's
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
```
5. Write the rule as a Python function f and check f(demo input) == demo output for every demo pair. Submit only when all match, pasting the printed json.dumps(f(G['Test input'])). If one mismatches, fix f or request another demo; never resubmit a grid already judged wrong.
6. Once f matches every demo, submit instead of requesting more demos.

def arm_analysis(g,o,label):
    bg,objs=components(g)
    byc=defaultdict(list)
    for c,cl in objs: byc[c].append(cl)
    chc={(y,x) for y in range(len(g)) for x in range(len(g[0])) if g[y][x]!=o[y][x]}
    rec=[(c,cl) for c,cl in objs if chc & set(cl)][0]
    recsib=[(c,cl) for c,cl in objs if skey(cl)==skey(rec[1]) and cl!=rec[1]][0]
    Ls=[(c,cl) for c,cl in objs if isL(cl) and len(cl)>=3 and len(byc[c])==1]
    tc,Lcl=max(Ls,key=lambda t:len(t[1]))
    Lcl=sorted(Lcl)
    corner=max(Lcl,key=lambda p:sum(1 for q in Lcl if abs(p[0]-q[0])+abs(p[1]-q[1])==1))
    ys=[y for y,x in Lcl]; xs=[x for y,x in Lcl]
    # arms: vertical = cells sharing corner column, horizontal = sharing corner row
    varm=[p for p in Lcl if p[1]==corner[1]]; harm=[p for p in Lcl if p[0]==corner[0]]
    vtip = varm[0] if varm[0][0]>varm[-1][0] else varm[-1]
    htip = harm[0] if abs(harm[0][1]-corner[1])>abs(harm[-1][1]-corner[1]) else harm[-1]
    near, far = (recsib, rec) if mind(recsib[1],Lcl)<mind(rec[1],Lcl) else (rec, recsib)
    d,p,q = min(((math.dist(pp,qq),pp,qq) for pp in near[1] for qq in Lcl))
    istip = q in (vtip,htip)
    # is near member on the line of an arm?
    online = any(pp[1]==corner[1] or pp[0]==corner[0] for pp in near[1])
    print(f"{label}: L{tc} corner={corner} vtip={vtip} htip={htip} | near {near[0]} closestL={q} tip?={istip} nearOnArmLine={online} delta=({p[0]-q[0]},{p[1]-q[1]})")
for idx,(g_,o_) in enumerate(alldemos): arm_analysis(g_,o_,f'demo{idx}')

def eval_variant(demos, use_centroid=True, arrow_sel='maxsize'):
    ok=0; details=[]
    for din,dout in demos:
        bg_,objs_=components(din)
        cs_=defaultdict(list)
        for cc,cl in objs_: cs_[skey(cl)].append((cc,cl))
        Ls_=[(cc,cl) for cc,cl in objs_ if isL(cl)]
        if not Ls_: details.append(('noL',)); continue
        if arrow_sel=='maxsize': arrow=max(Ls_,key=lambda t: len(t[1]))
        else: arrow=Ls_[0]
        def nd(cl):
            if use_centroid:
                cy=sum(r for r,_ in cl)/len(cl); cx=sum(c for _,c in cl)/len(cl)
                ay=sum(r for r,_ in arrow[1])/len(arrow[1]); ax=sum(c for _,c in arrow[1])/len(arrow[1])
                return math.hypot(cy-ay,cx-ax)
            return cdist(cl,arrow[1])
        cands_=[]
        for kk,vv in cs_.items():
            if len(vv)==2:
                (a0,cl0),(a1,cl1)=vv
                n0,n1=nd(cl0),nd(cl1)
                nearc,farc=(cl0,cl1) if n0<n1 else (cl1,cl0)
                cands_.append((min(n0,n1),farc,nd(farc),a0,a1))
        if not cands_: details.append(('noclass',)); continue
        cands_.sort()
        _,farc,_,a0,a1=cands_[0]
        o=[r[:] for r in din]
        for r_,c_ in farc: o[r_][c_]=arrow[0]
        good = o==dout
        ok+=good
        details.append((good,[c for c,_ in cs_[skey(farc)] if (c,skey([ (r,c) for r,c in farc]))] , a0,a1,arrow[0],[farc[0]][0]))
    return ok, details

def solid_rect(cl):
    rs=[r for r,_ in cl]; cs_=[c for _,c in cl]
    return len(cl)==(max(rs)-min(rs)+1)*(max(cs_)-min(cs_)+1)
def trueL(cl):
    if len(cl)<3: return False
    rs=[r for r,_ in cl]; cs_=[c for _,c in cl]
    if len(cl)==(max(rs)-min(rs)+1) or len(cl)==(max(cs_)-min(cs_)+1): return False  # straight bar
    # corner test: exists cell with arms
    S=set(cl)
    for (r,c) in cl:
        armv=sum(1 for d in (1,2,3) if (r+d,c) in S or (r-d,c) in S)
        armh=sum(1 for d in (1,2,3) if (r,c+d) in S or (r,c-d) in S)
        # proper L: two perpendicular segments from corner
        up=(r-1,c) in S or (r+1,c) in S
        side=(r,c-1) in S or (r,c+1) in S

def run_rule_fix(din, arrow_cl, metric='centroid', filt=None, rot=False, allow=True):
    acol=din[arrow_cl[0][0]][arrow_cl[0][1]]
    keyf = rotkey if rot else skey
    D=collections.defaultdict(list)
    for cc,cl in components(din)[1]: D[keyf(cl)].append(cl)

    for k,mem in D.items():
        if len(mem)!=2: continue
        if not allow and any(len(m)==1 for m in mem): continue
        ds=[near_mind(m,arrow_cl) if metric=='mind' else near_cen(m,arrow_cl) for m in mem]
        if filt is not None and min(ds)>filt+1e-9: continue
        far=mem[0] if ds[0]>=ds[1] else mem[1]
        cands.append((min(ds), far))
    if not cands: return 'NOCHANGE'
    cands.sort(key=lambda t:t[0])
    return [(r,c,acol) for r,c in cands[0][1]]
